To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
unattended fearful face images capture more attentional resources on a low cognitive demand task than neutral faces, and the effect of fearful faces was not observed on a high cognitive demand task.
fearful faces can automatically capture attention resources if the cognitive load of the task is not high.
the processing of unattended fearful faces is facilitated on a low cognitive demand task, whereas the processing of unattached neutral faces is not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
automatic attention capture and its effects on cognitive performance.
the effects of exposure to emotional stimuli on automatic attention while performing low and high cognitive load tasks.
the automatic processing of facial expressions of emotions under unattended conditions, and the results provide a better understanding of how the automatic attention system works.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fearful faces capture attention automatically if attention resources are available, but not if they are not.
the automaticity of the emotional face effect is a function of the availability of attention resources.
emotional faces could automatically capture the attention resources of the human brain, but only under the unattended conditions when the cognitive demand of the ongoing task is low.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
emotional faces are processed in a bottom-up, automatic fashion, and the automatic processing is affected by cognitive load and attention resources.
fearful faces are more likely to attract attention than neutral faces when the cognitive load of a concurrent task is low.

the attentional resources available for processing the unattended emotional facial expression were not only determined by the cognitive task demand but also the emotional valence and intensity of the unattended facial expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fearful faces can automatically capture attention if there is any residue of attention resources available under the unattend condition.
the attention resources available under the unattentive condition can be allocated to the processing of fearful faces.
the automaticity of attention capture by fearful faces is not a fixed characteristic of human beings, but depends on the availability of attention resources.
